subject.title: Vertex beta INVALID_ARGUMENT can wedge long sessions without actionable recovery

question: Should OpenClaw handle the LiteLLM/Vertex beta generic `INVALID_ARGUMENT` shape as a narrow provider-owned recovery case, and what recovery action should it take after classification?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the same status can represent multiple provider contract failures, so maintainers need to choose the permanent classifier boundary and recovery behavior before automation changes it.

options.title: Narrow provider-owned recovery
options.body: Add LiteLLM/Google hook classification only for the observed Vertex beta envelope and surface an actionable recoverable message while preserving generic handling for other invalid arguments.

options.title: Wait for live repro
options.body: Keep the issue open until a credentialed LiteLLM Vertex beta repro identifies whether the bad history, route, model, or payload shape should drive recovery.

options.title: Decline automatic recovery
options.body: Keep generic invalid arguments as non-recoverable provider failures and only improve redacted diagnostics so operators can reset or change route manually.

recommendation.title: Narrow provider-owned recovery
recommendation.body: Add LiteLLM/Google hook classification only for the observed Vertex beta envelope and surface an actionable recoverable message while preserving generic handling for other invalid arguments.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged and reviewed the adjacent provider-error classifier work and already flagged that this area needed more complete normalization judgment.
